channel.title: Los Angeles Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Los Angeles Times (latimes.com)

item.title: Activists celebrate as immigration agents depart Terminal Island. 'The people kicked them out'
item.description: Federal immigration agents departed from the Coast Guard site at Terminal Island in San Pedro, which they had used as a base for months while the Trump administration conducted immigration raids across Southern California.

item.title: In 50-year fight to protect California's coast, they're the real McCoys, still at it in their 80s
item.description: Imperial Beach couple Mike and Patricia McCoy have inspired generations of coastal conservationists.

item.title: L.A. County wants a healthcare sales tax. Cities are in revolt
item.description: County supervisors say it's the only way to keep the health system from collapse. Cities have their doubts.

item.title: L.A. streetlights take a year to fix. Council members say solar power is the answer
item.description: Broken streetlights have emerged as a hot-button issue in this year’s election, with council members scrambling to find ways to restore them.

item.title: Strong storm set to pummel L.A. with heavy rains, flooding and beach hazards
item.description: A strong storm system is set to hit Southern California starting Sunday, bringing potential thunderstorms, damaging winds and dangerous surf.

item.title: Sprawling network of brothels in Ventura and L.A. counties busted by authorities
item.description: A massive Southern California brothel ring was busted by authorities, leading to two arrests, officials said.

item.title: A wolf came to L.A. looking for love. On Valentine's Day, she's moved on
item.description: The 3-year-old wolf — known as BEY03F — made history when she entered L.A. County last weekend. But she's spending the romantic holiday in Kern County.

item.title: Who pays for Newsom's travel? Hint: It's not always taxpayers
item.description: Gov. Gavin Newsom's international travel is paid for by the California State Protocol Foundation, a nonprofit that is funded primarily by corporate donations and run by a board Newsom appoints.

item.title: Casey Wasserman to sell his talent agency following Epstein fallout
item.description: Casey Wasserman is selling his talent agency after documents revealed racy emails he exchanged with Jeffrey Epstein's companion years ago. Wasserman will remain leader of the LA28 Olympic Committee, which publicly backed him despite the uproar.

item.title: Nancy Guthrie kidnapping investigation draws scrutiny as case drags on
item.description: Criticism of the local sheriff's department's handling of the case has mounted, with questions raised about its ability to handle such a high-profile, complex crime under the harsh media spotlight.
